title: Shared module settings, permissions and resources
objective: Give trusted modules host-owned settings, secure credentials, scoped consent, bounded activation/downloads and durable derived artifacts through the same discoverable service used by the desktop and API.
context_summary: Proposed follow-up to the implemented linked-module contract. This plan supplies generic capabilities needed by Corrections and future modules, while leaving third-party executable loading to a separately measured extension. Owner decisions on consent and provider policy precede implementation.

tasks.description: Freeze the shared capability and consent contract with the owner.
extra_context: Planning only; implementation starts only after the owner accepts the proposed defaults. Keep unresolved provider and consent tradeoffs as proposals.

context_links.label: Capability proposal
context_links.relevance: Scope, security boundary, API semantics and owner choices.

acceptance_criteria: Record accepted setting scopes, first-use/per-asset consent rule, revocation behavior, secret-storage failure policy and local versus remote endpoint rules.
Specify current-shape errors, versioning, data migration refusal and external-loader boundary without treating declarations as a sandbox.

steps: Review each decision against module and catalog invariants and resolve consequential owner choices.
Confirm every future operation has an API equivalent and no unresolved policy is silently accepted.
expected_results: One reviewed contract and an explicit list of any decisions still blocking implementation.

tasks.description: Extend module descriptors and API discovery with typed settings, capability declarations and activation metadata.
extra_context: Descriptor registration stays cheap and does no I/O; use named provider profiles and typed adapters rather than arbitrary URL templates.
acceptance_criteria: Malformed setting IDs, kinds, defaults, capabilities, endpoint constraints and duplicate profile IDs fail registration with named errors.
schema.list and module.list expose the same non-secret definitions the desktop uses; no key value appears in descriptors.
Registration, catalog reopen and module listing cause no network, file or model activity.

steps: Exercise accepted/rejected descriptors and serialized discovery.
Verify registration has no resource side effects.
expected_results: A proof descriptor is discoverable with exact schemas and no side effects.

tasks.description: Implement host-owned user settings and secret storage with revisions and redaction.
extra_context: The first native target is macOS Keychain; plan Windows Credential Manager and Linux Secret Service without claiming untested portability.
Never store credentials in the catalog, recipe, log, event or plain configuration.

context_links.label: Capability proposal
context_links.relevance: Settings shape, secure store and redaction.

acceptance_criteria: Atomic non-secret writes, revision conflicts and request retries behave identically for UI and API clients; unsupported configuration is retained and rejected.
Secret set/clear/read-presence works with the OS store; locked/unavailable storage fails explicitly with no plaintext fallback.
Schemas, state, events, errors, logs and copied requests redact secret values; reopen and provider-profile removal are covered.

steps: Use a fake secure store for deterministic errors and a native macOS secure-store journey.
Scan protocol and evidence outputs for test secret sentinels.
expected_results: Settings survive restart; no secret bytes escape through an observable surface.

tasks.description: Implement scoped permission grants and protected network/file transports.
extra_context: Distinguish app consent from an OS prompt; a service client can grant only an exact authenticated request scope.

context_links.label: Capability proposal
context_links.relevance: Consent, revocation, endpoint and file rules.

context_links.label: Development evidence
context_links.relevance: Background-only native checks and scope of verification.

acceptance_criteria: First gated operation returns a precise consent request; an ordinary edit client cannot self-grant, and explicit privileged grant, denial, revocation and endpoint change have observable status through UI/API.
Transport enforces HTTPS/explicit loopback, destination/redirect rules, payload and time limits, path scope and changed-file detection.
Revocation prevents new work and cancels affected pending work; it preserves existing recipes and accepted artifacts.

steps: Use fake endpoints and selected-file fixtures for redirects, rebinding/private IP, path traversal, symlinks, oversize and revoke races.
Inspect native consent/error UI and API event parity.
expected_results: Unapproved bytes never leave or enter the granted scope, and denials remain recoverable.

tasks.description: Add bounded module activation and resource job lifecycle to the host.
extra_context: Activation is requested, never triggered by discovery or catalog reopen; module-specific work runs on a worker.

context_links.label: Performance rules
context_links.relevance: Owner thread, queue and resource limits.

acceptance_criteria: Activate/deactivate/status and resource job operations are schema-described and return prompt, cancellable status with progress and structured errors.
One active plus bounded pending work or an equivalently measured limit prevents unbounded CPU/memory; idle workers sleep and cancellation releases resources.
UI/owner threads perform no model loading, hashing, download or inference; missing settings/grants are reported before the worker starts.

steps: Test blocked, cancelled, superseded and completed activation with a synthetic slow loader.
Measure owner response and idle state on the M4.
expected_results: Discovery is inert, activation is bounded, and clients observe one consistent lifecycle.

tasks.description: Implement verified opt-in model/resource installation and removal.
extra_context: This is host-managed data download, not arbitrary module code execution or an app auto-updater.
acceptance_criteria: User-initiated pinned downloads and selected local copies enforce expected size, SHA-256, format and storage quota before atomic publish.
Interrupted, corrupt, short, oversized, redirected and disk-full downloads leave no installed resource or modified source file; status is restart-safe.
Model storage and Remove are visible; removal frees resources but cannot make an accepted correction disappear.
Artifact licenses and provenance are recorded without claiming the deferred manual audit is complete.

steps: Serve fixed local test artifacts and failures, then exercise install/remove via API and desktop.
expected_results: Only verified resources become installed, and failed installs leave clean state.

tasks.description: Build immutable derived-artifact storage with history reachability and crash recovery.
extra_context: This is a generic host primitive for future generated edits, separate from module-private mutable state and downloaded weights.
acceptance_criteria: A recipe commit can reference a checksum-verified immutable artifact by opaque ID and atomically retain the reference across catalog restart.
Every history branch, version, preview and restore keeps reachable artifacts; GC affects only disposable or provably unreachable files.
Missing/corrupt referenced bytes cause explicit render/sample/export failures without rewriting any recipe; source bytes remain identical.

Moving the catalog and its adjacent managed-artifact directory together preserves every referenced hash; copying only the SQLite file fails explicitly, and selecting a moved artifact directory verifies hashes before use.

steps: Inject crashes before/after artifact publish and catalog commit.
Test history branching, undo, restore, duplicate content, missing/corrupt file, reachability and catalog-plus-artifact relocation.
expected_results: No committed snapshot points at an unpublished artifact; no retained entry loses its pixels.

tasks.description: Prove the full capability path with a tiny linked module and generated UI/API controls.
extra_context: The proof module is a test fixture, not a user-facing model integration; use background editor launches.

context_links.label: Capability proposal
context_links.relevance: Required proof module and parity evidence.

acceptance_criteria: One test module demonstrates non-secret and secret settings, a selected-file read, pinned download, activation, permission grants and a committed artifact.
Desktop and JSON invoke the same operations with matching statuses/errors, including headless consent_required and cancellation.
Rendered capture, correlated state and logs show progress, denial, ready and failure states; no credentials appear in captures.

steps: Run the proof against an isolated catalog and fake endpoint in the background editor.
Compare module.list/schema.list and UI controls, then inspect state, logs and captures.
commands: cargo run --release --locked --package xtask -- verify --tier rendered --output NEW_DIR
expected_results: The proof lifecycle and settings work identically in UI and API and meet rendered evidence rules.

tasks.description: Measure, document and qualify the shared framework on the M4.
extra_context: A skipped or VM check is not native evidence; do not claim Windows/Linux secure-store behavior before native checks.

context_links.label: Feature status
context_links.relevance: Only implemented behavior is marked delivered.

acceptance_criteria: Record cold registration, activation, idle CPU, memory, download disk and cancellation with host/build/fixture scope and a before/after comparison.
Run quick, rendered and timing at integration and full before a milestone claim; report failures and skipped checks exactly.
Update current module/API design, feature status and user guide to shipped behavior and remaining platform limits.

steps: Run the tiered verifier and inspect its summaries, rendered artifacts and native timing.
Review all performance-rules checklist questions and documentation.
commands: cargo run --release --locked --package xtask -- verify --tier full --output NEW_DIR
expected_results: Native M4 qualification has explicit evidence and no unsupported platform, privacy or speed claim.
